title: Resource surface model and operator contracts
summary: Working notes describing a compact, operator-friendly resource surface and REST API conventions for the control plane. Focus: stable identity, region/cluster affinity, routing labels, idempotent writes, and lightweight reconciliation semantics for multi-region deployments.
motivation: We need a small, consistent set of primitives that teams can adopt without heavy client-side orchestration. Current designs scatter tenancy and region routing across multiple resources; this doc proposes a single surface per customer-facing logical resource plus a thin routing layer expressed as attributes so the control plane can make deterministic routing and reconciliation decisions.
principles: 1) Single canonical resource per logical entity (no duplicate shims). 2) Stable, opaque IDs are primary keys; names are mutable. 3) Routing is expressed as policy attributes rather than separate objects. 4) CRUD APIs are idempotent and support optimistic concurrency with etags. 5) Minimal eventual-consistency bounds: writes converge within a bounded reconciliation window and provide retries/fallbacks for regional failures.
resource_surface_overview: Surface = ResourceRecord (top-level) + EnvironmentAttachment(s) + RegionBinding(s). ResourceRecord contains owner, type, spec blob (opaque but versioned), and an ownership namespace id. EnvironmentAttachment expresses logical environment (dev/stage/prod) settings. RegionBinding is small - contains region, preferred clusters, soft capacity hints, and allowed fallback tiers.
identity_and_names:
- id: UUIDv4, opaque primary id.
- external_name: human-readable (not unique).
- natural_key: optional tuple (customer_id, external_name) used only for idempotent create attempts.
- resource_version: monotonically increasing token (etag) for optimistic concurrency.
routing_model:
Routing modeled as attributes on ResourceRecord and RegionBinding:
- routing_policy: one of {latency-first, cost-first, region-strict, affinity}.
- affinity_tags: list of tokens used to match clusters (e.g., gpu-v100, ssd-local).
- fallback_order: ordered list of fallback region ids.
Control plane uses policy + real-time capacity signals to resolve a target cluster. Policy evaluation is deterministic and versioned so route decisions can be replayed during audits.
api_contracts_summary:
- POST /v1/resources: Create-if-not-exists using natural_key and idempotency-token header; returns 201 or 200 with existing resource.
- GET /v1/resources/{id}: Returns canonical resource and region bindings.
- PATCH /v1/resources/{id}: Partial update. Requires If-Match: etag or will fail with 412.
- PUT /v1/resources/{id}/bindings/{region}: Upsert region binding; idempotent.
- DELETE /v1/resources/{id}: Soft-delete (tombstone) by default; deletion must be confirmed via query param and audited.
- List endpoints support cursor pagination and region/tenant filters.
Common headers: Idempotency-Key, If-Match, X-Client-Intent (for routing hints).
idempotency_and_conflicts: Guidelines: clients SHOULD provide Idempotency-Key for creates. Server generates resource id on first accepted create and returns location. If natural_key conflict: return 409 with existing id. PATCH requires If-Match; absent header triggers read-modify-write with server-assigned etag and a warning header. Deletes set tombstone=true and leave minimal record for 7 days for reconciliation.
reconciliation_and_event_model:
- Write path: API -> consistent write to primary region store -> fan-out change event to regional replicas.
- Reconciliation loop: region replica compares incoming resource_version and applies deltas; if missing dependencies, mark binding state=Pending with reason.
- Events are versioned; retries are idempotent.
- Consumer of events should use (resource_id, resource_version) as idempotency key when applying.
crud_patterns_and_examples:
Create pattern: client posts natural_key + spec + routing hints + Idempotency-Key. Server returns 201 (created) or 200 (existing).
Update pattern: patch spec + If-Match header with retry-on-412 logic. Server merges known-updatable fields and rejects incompatible spec shape with 422.
Binding changes: clients call PUT /bindings to change region affinity; operation is local to resource and reconciles asynchronously to cluster allocation.
Delete pattern: soft-delete then background purge after retention window. Clients may request hard-delete with admin scope and must supply delete-confirm=true.
operational_considerations:
- Audit trail: every mutate operation emits (who, when, why, client-intent) in an audit store.
- Metrics to track: apply-latency, reconciliation-delay, conflicting-writes-rate, tombstone-count-by-region.
- Backpressure: when regional capacity is low, mark bindings with state=Degraded and provide 'suggested-fallback' header to callers.
- Rollouts: support canary routing via binding flags and 'percent_routing' field for gradual traffic shifts.
upgrade_and_migration_notes:
- Schema evolution: spec blob is opaque; schema versions are declared as top-level metadata. Old control-plane versions must tolerate unknown fields.
- Migration: add new region bindings as new records rather than moving existing ones. Migration tool will materialize region-binding records and stamp resource_version increments.
- Deprecation policy: announce breaking changes 30 days, provide automated migration scripts for common patterns.
audit_and_safety:
- Tombstone records retained for 7 days (configurable per-tenant) to allow cross-region reconciliation and accidental delete recovery.
- Deletion requires two-step confirmation for resources tagged as 'production' and admin scope.
- Safe-mode: control plane exposes a read-only snapshot endpoint for disaster recovery and forensic replay.
open_questions:
- How aggressively should the control plane normalize affinity tags vs freeform labels? (tradeoff: flexibility vs matching complexity).
- Should fallback_order be evaluated at write time or at routing time? Write-time evaluation simplifies replay but may become stale.
- Do we need a dedicated RoutingPolicy resource to allow dynamic updates independent of ResourceRecord? Currently leaning no to keep surface small.
next_steps: 1) Prototype minimal server-side evaluation of routing_policy (latency-first + region-strict). 2) Implement ETag/If-Match enforcement and Idempotency-Key handling for creates. 3) Build a small migration tool for materializing region-binding records. 4) Draft API docs and an example SDK helper for retries/backoff.
notes_to_reviewers: Feedback wanted on: resource_version semantics, tombstone retention defaults, and whether 'spec' should be partially typed for common resource types. Also sanity-check the idempotency flows against existing infra (see linked PR).
